label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. If a cookie banner offers no way to decline that works, accept it, report that as a problem, and carry on. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: Reached the payment step. Stopped there: nothing was paid.

findings.problem: After pressing Add to cart nothing was announced: the button just became disabled and the cart link still said cart empty. The Added to your cart dialog only showed up after I re-read the page, so I did not know if the add worked.

element.name: Add to cart, opens in modal

findings.problem: The cart link kept saying cart empty even after an item was added, which is misleading.

element.name: cart empty: click to Open cart

findings.problem: Several controls have unclear names: a close button in the cart dialog has no name at all, three Add to cart buttons for suggested items do not say which product they add, and the price line reads As low as $/week with . with the amounts missing.

Every collection card is one huge link whose name is a long run of text, so the product names, prices and ratings are hard to tell apart; the Snug card is only reachable as a small link far below them.

On checkout the Pay now button is disabled with no explanation of what is missing, the marketing opt-in checkbox is pre-checked, and the payment fields sit in separate iframes that are hard to tell apart.
